case.goal: Pin down the log/slog Handler contract that custom and third-party handlers have to honour
contract: assert JSONHandler writes time, level and msg in that order under slog's built-in key constants
assert the JSON timestamp is RFC3339Nano with a variable-length fraction, while TextHandler and tint pad a time attribute to exactly three digits
assert a zero Record.Time drops the timestamp field entirely
assert ReplaceAttr renames the level and message keys and drops a field by returning a zero Attr
assert a ReplaceAttr without a len(groups) guard renames a user attribute named msg inside a group as well
assert the guard still cannot protect the built-in msg from a top-level attribute of the same name: the record carries two message keys and the JSON decoder keeps the last
assert only a zero Attr drops a field, while an empty value or an empty key is still written out
assert ReplaceAttr is called for the built-ins with no open groups and for a group's contents with the group path, never for the group attr itself
assert WithGroup nests later attributes, an empty group is omitted, and WithGroup with an empty name is a no-op
assert JSONHandler ignores fmt.Stringer and json-marshals the struct, while LogValue wins on both handlers
assert Handler.Enabled is consulted and Handle is skipped when the level is disabled
assert LogValue does not run for a disabled level but plain call arguments are evaluated anyway, and only an explicit Enabled guard skips them
assert a LogValuer passed to With is resolved once, at With time, and not again per record
assert WithAttrs and WithGroup each return a new handler, so a child logger's attrs and open group reach neither the parent nor a sibling
assert tint follows the same ReplaceAttr, group and LogValuer contract but formats a Stringer with %+v and writes ANSI escapes to a non-terminal unless NoColor is set
assert tint.NewHandler is the constructor deprecated in v1.2.0 and produces output identical to tint.NewTextHandler
